title: AI agents don’t log in like people. That problem just sold for $1bn.
excerpt: Every AI agent a company switches on needs an identity to log in and reach data. Enterprises now run millions of them, with almost no way to keep track. That gap just sold for $1bn. content_html:
Every AI agent a company switches on needs an identity to log in and reach data. Enterprises now run millions of them, with almost no way to keep track. That gap just sold for $1bn.

The data-security firm Cyera has agreed to buy Oasis Security for around $1bn, the Wall Street Journal first reported. It is a cash-and-stock deal, roughly $700m of it in cash. The companies expect it to close later this year.

Buying the ‘non-human identity’ layer

Cyera knows what data a company holds, and what is sensitive. Oasis governs “non-human identities,” the accounts that machines and AI agents use to reach that data. Put the two together, Cyera says, and you get one system deciding what every human, machine and agent can see and do.

That is the pitch, and the timing is the argument. Non-human identities inside big companies grew nearly 500% in six months, Cyera says, and are now the fastest-growing account type in the enterprise. Most firms run identity tools designed for humans, not for software that spins up thousands of agents.

A cyber land grab

The deal is the biggest yet in a scramble to secure AI agents. Money is pouring into the category, from Neo’s $100m raise to smaller bets like NeuralTrust’s seed round, TechCrunch reported. Oasis, founded only in 2022, reckons it is the fastest cybersecurity company ever to go from launch to a $1bn sale.

It also fits a wider wave. Cybersecurity dealmaking is heading for a record year. Cyera is not the only buyer rolling up smaller firms to build an all-in-one AI-security platform.

Growth bought, not earned

Cyera can afford the spree because investors keep funding it. It raised $600m in June at a $12bn valuation, and has now taken in about $2.3bn in total, CRN reported. Oasis is its fifth acquisition in months, after Genie Security, Ryft, Trail Security and others.

There is a caveat under the momentum. Cyera is still unprofitable, and its $12bn price tag sits at roughly 80 times revenue. The thesis also rests on millions of agents that mostly have not arrived yet. The bet is that they will, and that someone has to decide what each one can touch.

content_html_zh:
公司启用的每个人工智能代理都需要一个身份来登录和访问数据。 企业现在运行着数以百万计的数据，但几乎没有办法进行跟踪。 这一缺口刚刚以 10 亿美元的价格出售。

据《华尔街日报》首先报道，数据安全公司 Cyera 已同意以约 10 亿美元收购 Oasis Security。 这是一项现金加股票的交易，其中现金约 7 亿美元。 两家公司预计该工厂将于今年晚些时候关闭。

购买“非人类身份”层

Cyera 知道公司持有哪些数据以及哪些数据是敏感的。 Oasis 管理“非人类身份”，即机器和人工智能代理用来获取数据的帐户。 Cyera 说，将两者结合在一起，你就会得到一个系统来决定每个人、机器和代理可以看到什么和做什么。

这就是基调，而时机就是争论。 Cyera 表示，大公司内部的非人类身份在六个月内增长了近 500%，目前是企业中增长最快的帐户类型。 大多数公司运行的身份识别工具是为人类设计的，而不是为启动数千个代理的软件设计的。

网络抢地

这笔交易是人工智能代理争夺战中迄今为止规模最大的一笔交易。 据 TechCrunch 报道，资金正在涌入该类别，从 Neo 的 1 亿美元融资到 NeuralTrust 种子轮等较小规模的投资。 Oasis 于 2022 年才成立，它认为自己是有史以来从成立到销售额达到 10 亿美元最快的网络安全公司。

它还适合更宽的波浪。 网络安全交易将迎来创纪录的一年。 Cyera 并不是唯一一家联合小公司打造一体化人工智能安全平台的买家。

增长是买来的，不是赚来的

Cyera 有能力承担这场狂欢，因为投资者不断为其提供资金。 据 CRN 报道，该公司 6 月份以 120 亿美元的估值筹集了 6 亿美元，目前融资总额约为 23 亿美元。 Oasis 是继 Genie Security、Ryft、Trail Security 等公司之后数月内第五次收购。

在这种势头之下有一个警告。 Cyera 仍未盈利，其 120 亿美元的标价约为收入的 80 倍。 该论文还建立在数以百万计尚未到达的特工身上。 打赌他们会这么做，而且必须有人决定每个人可以触摸什么。
